target_customer: Satellite operators, aviation and mobility connectivity providers and defense buyers that need low cost flat panel satcom user terminals
problem: User terminals for satellite internet are large, power hungry and expensive, which limits adoption of satellite broadband for moving users and consumers.
business_model: Hardware sales of flat panel antenna terminals plus strategic development programs with satellite operators
product_category: Satcom user terminals, active electronically scanned flat panel antennas

founders.name: Siamak Ebadi
prior_employers: SpaceX (team that built the first Starlink satellites)
Astranis (lead RF antenna engineer on satellite payloads from 2018)
founders.background_notes: Prior employers from the Payload article on the rebrand. Education not found in sources opened. YC page lists him as the only founder.

competitors.name: Phasor
competitors.what: Electronically steered flat panel Ku-band antennas for aviation and maritime
competitors.traction_then: Partnerships with Intelsat, Gogo and maritime providers in beta testing

technical_complexity.rationale: Phased array flat panel terminals need custom RF chips, antenna design and low cost manufacturing, which is hardware research at the edge for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Deep RF and manufacturing know-how is hard to copy, but several funded rivals pursued the same flat panel approach.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Phasor was acquired by Hanwha Systems in June 2020 per CB Insights; no incumbent copied or bought Farcast as of the sources read. Strategic investors Lockheed Martin, Telesat and Gogo invested in 2025.

market_need_then: Satellite broadband constellations were being built in 2019 and 2020 and terminal cost and size were widely seen as the bottleneck, which the founder saw first hand at Astranis.

branding.name_origin: The original name UTVate blended user terminal and innovate (Payload, March 2025). Farcast was chosen in 2025 because the old name did not clearly convey the mission; no source explains the word itself.
branding.domain_note: Company now uses farcast.com; acquisition history of the domain not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain engineering tone: enabling global access to satellite internet

rebrands.why: Founder said the UTVate name did not clearly convey the mission to a wider customer base ahead of full production

brand_strength.rationale: Little brand press beyond trade coverage of the rebrand; the old name was a coined acronym blend that the company itself dropped.

outcome_analysis: Farcast remains active and is entering a 2026 production ramp. It raised from venture funds (about 13.6M by March 2025 per Payload) and then took strategic money from Lockheed Martin, Telesat and Gogo, which signals customer pull from satellite operators. The founder came from SpaceX and Astranis, matching the problem. The risk is hardware execution and a long path to volume production.
notes: Total raised conflicts: 13.6M (Payload, Mar 2025), 23.6M (Satellite Today, Dec 2025), 37.8M with a 16M Series A (Caplight, unverified, not recorded). Seed date and amount not found; a tracker reported a 2020 pre-seed of 572K, unverified. Only one competitor sourced near the batch (Phasor 2015 article); Kymeta and ThinKom existed but no dated source was opened. Outcome search for shutdown or layoffs returned nothing relevant.
